audit.why: 46.87% over 1276 games, TRICKY 7/10: Mel bullies pre-6, Ekko takes over with Chronobreak and roams. Ratings fit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Layers disagree at Level 6: full phases[4].side=Ekko but content win[4]=Mel, and whys[4] describes level 5 ('he still has no Chronobreak') under the Level 6 row. Rows 0-3 and 5-6 in the full layer are blanket 'Skill'.
audit.why: Content's own spikes[1] and late prose say 6 flips the lane (Chronobreak dive with rewind safety net). Packet levelChart[4]=Mel looks stale for the same reason its own defect note flags.
audit.corrected: win[4] Mel->Ekko with rewritten whys[4]; full rows 0-3 -> Mel, 4-6 -> Ekko with matching whys/ratings.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns has no digits and misses that his W shields him in the anomaly (missingInteractions: shield-absorbs-burst); dontsFull[2].d is pasted tradeBad and never names the non-projectiles its title promises; his E auto-reset wind-up tell is absent from the page.
audit.why: Chronobreak 110s rank 1 (untargetable + heals — anti-heal and hold-your-execute case), W 22s with shield+stun, Q Timewinder 9s is his only true projectile; W's projectile flag contradicts its anomaly description so it is treated as non-reflectable.
audit.corrected: Numbers and W-shield warning added to cooldowns; dontsFull[2].d now lists the non-projectiles; bleed bullets rewritten.

edits.before: At 5 he still has no Chronobreak, so your zone control and snare stay ahead.
edits.after: At 6 Chronobreak gives him a dive with a rewind — his all-in now beats yours.

edits.before: Golden Eclipse online — the execute threshold turns your chip war into a countdown he can see.
edits.after: Chronobreak online: he dives with a rewind safety net and his W-stun all-in turns lethal.

edits.before: Luden's spike: snare-volley chunks half bars and the execute cleans the remainder. Force contacts.
edits.after: His tempo-item spike snowballs roams and all-ins — Chronobreak erases your kill pressure.

edits.before: Late Mel is a counter-artillery battery: reflect their poke, snare their dive, and execute the chipped.
edits.after: Teamfight Ekko flanks with the W stun and resets on R — hold your snare to peel Phase Dive off you.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — 110s at rank 1; it erases your kill and heals him, so save final damage for after it. - His W is 22s and shields him inside the anomaly — force it before you commit. - Your W Rebuttal has one job: the moment it all goes wrong.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: The glow makes his Q return-hit a risk even up close — hold ground behind it and farm while he waits the barrier out.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: His W stun zone, Phase Dive and Chronobreak are not projectiles — Rebuttal returns Timewinder only, never the all-in behind it.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Ekko wins by layering the W stun under Phase Dive, diving on Chronobreak's safety net, and roaming on tempo.

notes: win[4] flipped Mel->Ekko: content's own level-6 prose, the full layer's existing side, and the WR defect note all give 6 to Ekko; whys[4] was describing level 5.
